Container.Name: localizer
Container.Overview:
Localizer gives every Docker container on your server a name.
Map 192.168.1.50:8080 to openwebui.local, 192.168.1.50:8989 to sonarr.local, and so on. Localizer runs a reverse proxy that routes by hostname and an mDNS responder that makes those .local names resolve across your LAN — no router, Pi-hole or hosts-file changes needed on any client. Other suffixes (home.arpa, internal, lan) work too.
With the Docker socket mapped in, "Refresh from Unraid" finds the containers you are running and keeps the tiles in step with them: new containers are offered, deleted ones flagged, moved ports shown — and nothing changes until you tick it. The launch screen has live up/down indicators, categories you can create, rename and drag between, and an edit button on every tile.
SETUP — THREE STEPS:
1. Give Localizer its OWN IP ADDRESS. Set Network Type to "Custom: br0" and enter a Fixed IP outside your DHCP pool. The Unraid webGUI already owns port 80 on the host, and mDNS needs real multicast, so the default bridge network will not work.
2. Attach a second network after the first start, in a terminal:
docker network connect bridge localizer
br0 is a macvlan or ipvlan network, and a container on it cannot reach its own host, so without this every mapped service reads as offline. Pressing Apply recreates the container and drops the attachment; to make it permanent, install unraid/localizer-bridge.sh from the project with the User Scripts plugin, scheduled At Startup of Array. Localizer reports it in its log and System tab if the attachment is missing.
3. The Docker Socket path is optional. It enables "Refresh from Unraid". Localizer only reads from it, but anything holding the socket can control Docker, and a read-only mount does not change that. Remove the path if you would rather not.
First run: browse to the IP you assigned and create your login. Nothing is preconfigured and there is no default password.
Container.Description: Gives every Docker container a .local name: reverse proxy, mDNS responder, container discovery and a dashboard. Requires its own IP on br0.

Config.Name: Config Storage
Config.Description: Stores config.json — routes, categories, settings, cached icons and your login.

Config.Name: Docker Socket
Config.Description: Optional. Enables "Refresh from Unraid". Localizer only reads from it, but anything holding the socket can control Docker; a read-only mount does not change that.

Config.Name: HTTP Port
Config.Description: Port the proxy and web UI listen on. Leave at 80 so your URLs stay clean; the container has its own IP, so nothing else is using it.

Config.Name: mDNS Port
Config.Description: Multicast DNS. Leave at 5353 — clients will not find .local names on any other port.

Config.Name: HTTP_PORT
Config.Description: Must match the HTTP Port above.
